title: Date-effective table with as-of validTimeState select vs the unfiltered plain select
instruction: In the sandbox model, prove the date-effective select contract. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="date-effective") and get_knowledge(topic="select-statement"). Create: (1) a table DemoWorkerBonusRate (table group Main) made date-effective by setting ValidTimeStateFieldType = Date, so the table carries the ValidFrom/ValidTo date columns (use exactly those platform names — do NOT invent differently named period fields). Business fields: WorkerId (String, EDT Num, mandatory) and BonusRate (Real, EDT Percent); use the standard EDTs from the index rather than inventing new ones. Add the required unique alternate-key index BonusRateIdx keyed on WorkerId and satisfying the platform's valid-time-state key requirement (AllowDuplicates = No, AlternateKey = Yes, ValidTimeStateKey = Yes, ValidTimeStateMode = NoGap — a date-effective table does not build without this index). (2) a class DemoWorkerBonusRateService with public static methods: (a) `void addRate(Num _workerId, Percent _rate, date _validFrom, date _validTo)` - inserts one version, stamping ValidFrom/ValidTo from the arguments inside ttsbegin/ttscommit; (b) `Percent effectiveRate(Num _workerId, date _asOfDate)` - returns the BonusRate of the SINGLE version valid on _asOfDate via `select validTimeState(_asOfDate)`; validTimeState is a FindOption and must sit between select and the buffer; (c) `int versionCount(Num _workerId)` - a PLAIN select count for the worker that deliberately omits validTimeState, demonstrating the trap this case exists to teach: an unfiltered X++ select returns ALL versions, historical included (forms and Query objects filter to the current date automatically — X++ code is the odd one out). Adding validTimeState to (c), or hand-filtering (c) on ValidFrom/ValidTo, FAILS the case. Both objects must build with zero BP errors.
